title: pilot-pii-minimization-patterns-and-legal-checklist
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working note for SEs running short pilot projects (2–12 weeks) where customers want to limit PII exposure and get a DPA-addendum sketch that the legal team can iterate on. Focus: technical patterns that minimize PII in telemetry and model inputs, and a concise legal checklist and sample addendum language to accelerate SOC/contract reviews.

Audience:
- Solutions Engineers (primary)
- Customer Security/Legal reviewers
- Product/Privacy for input on operational guarantees

Context / assumptions:
- Typical pilot: sandboxed integration with customer app, up to ~100k tokens/day, not full production traffic.
- Options for deployment: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved), Private (VPC/on-prem). PII surface and controls differ by deployment.
- Customer requirement patterns we've seen: no raw PII retained, audit trail required but minimal, KMS for key material, 72-hour incident notification, right-to-delete for pilot data.

High-level minimization patterns (technical):
1) Client-side pseudonymization (recommended first line):
   - Replace direct identifiers (SSNs, emails, phone numbers) in the browser or server SDK before sending. Use reversible token mapping only when absolutely needed for end-to-end testing; otherwise use irreversible hashes (salted SHA-256) stored only by customer.
   - Provide a small mapping util in the pilot repo (example: se-scrub-util.js) with test-mode salt.

2) On-the-fly redaction & schema enforcement at the gateway:
   - For Hosted/Dedicated customers who must use Redwood routing, configure request pre-processing rules to reject or redact known PII JSON keys (e.g., email, ssn, card_number) before tokens hit the inference runtime.
   - Our gateway supports simple redaction rules and regex-based fields; document these in pilot-runbook.

3) Ephemeral context windows + ephemeral KV:
   - Avoid persisting full conversation history; use short context windows (2–5 turns) and implement scoped KV caches that expire immediately after the session.
   - For demos that require history, store only summary objects (no raw PII).

4) Token / telemetry minimization:
   - Limit telemetry to event-type + latency + coarse token counts. Never send full text as telemetry to Redwood-hosted analytics for POCs unless explicitly approved.
   - For Hosted API pilots, enable a telemetry opt-in flag on the account.

5) Deterministic hashing for lookup use-cases:
   - When pilots need to map incoming users to test personas, prefer deterministic hashes with customer-managed salt. Do not store the unhashed identifier in Redwood logs.

6) Customer-side KMS and envelope encryption (for Private/Dedicated):
   - Recommend customer-managed KMS for keys controlling KV/cache encryption. For Private deployments we can integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM.

Data categories and recommended retention (pilot defaults):
- Raw model inputs containing PII: retention = 0 days (do not persist). If persisted for debugging, retention <= 14 days and encrypted with customer KMS, access restricted to named SEs.
- Redacted inputs / summaries: retention = 30 days (default); can be shortened per customer.
- Audit logs (request timestamp, model id, route, token counts, SE notes): retention = 90 days (encrypted).
- Telemetry/metrics (aggregated): retention = 365 days (opt-in).
- Session keys / ephemeral KV: immediate expiry after session end (0–1 hour).

Sample retention matrix (text form):
- debug_payloads: 14 days (encryption, access: se-team)
- redacted_conversations: 30 days (encryption, access: customer+se)
- audit_trail: 90 days (immutable, encrypted)
- aggregated_metrics: 365 days

Operational controls & runbook checklist for SEs (pre-pilot):
- Confirm customer deployment choice and map controls accordingly (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- Provide the customer with the pilot scrub util and integration example.
- Turn on redaction rules at the gateway before the first test run.
- Agree on which artifacts SEs are allowed to store for debugging and obtain explicit written permission.
- Generate a test-only API key with scoped usage and TTL for the pilot.
- Configure KMS settings for Dedicated/Private pilots; verify CMK access with customer.
- Confirm incident notification SLA (e.g., 72 hours) and escalation contacts.

Legal checklist for DPA addendum (quick hits to include in pilot addendum):
- Purpose limitation: explicit statement that pilot data will only be used for the pilot and debugging by named parties.
- Retention caps: include the matrix above with explicit deletion guarantees and audit evidence.
- Data access: list named SEs and customer contacts; require written change requests for additional access.
- Encryption: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, and customer-managed KMS option.
- Subprocessors: short list for pilot (e.g., cloud provider regions used); commit to notify for changes.
- Cross-border transfers: declare regions and rely on SCCs or equivalent as needed.
- Incident notif: 72 hours for material breaches; 24 hours for confirmed exfiltration of PII.
- Right to delete / right to be forgotten: process and timeline (7 business days for pilot deletion confirmation).
- Audit & verification: sample audit evidence package (deletion logs, retention table, access logs) to be delivered at pilot close.
- Liability cap / indemnity: pilot-tier language (mutual, limited to fees paid for the pilot) — flag to legal for escalation.

Sample DPA addendum snippet (boilerplate starter; replace placeholders):
"POC Data Handling Addendum (pilot):
1) Scope: Data processed for purposes of the pilot between [Customer] and Redwood Inference.
2) Retention: Redwood will retain pilot artifacts only as specified in the attached retention matrix. Upon pilot termination, Redwood will delete customer data in accordance with Section X and provide a deletion certificate.
3) Access: Access to pilot artifacts is restricted to named SEs: [list] and authorized customer personnel. Any additional access requires customer prior written consent.
4) Encryption & KMS: All data in transit will use TLS 1.2+; data at rest will be encrypted using AES-256. For Dedicated/Private pilots, customer may provide KMS keys to control encryption.
5) Telemetry: No full-text telemetry will be collected by Redwood analytics for this pilot unless expressly agreed in writing.
6) Incident Notification: Redwood to notify customer of any confirmed data breach affecting pilot data within 72 hours of confirmation.
7) Deletion Certification: On request within 7 business days after pilot end, Redwood will provide a signed deletion certificate listing artifacts removed and timestamps.
"

Example operational notes (realistic SE-level):
- "Notes to self: when demoing with Acme Health, enable client-side mask for email/ssn. Add an extra logging toggle so we can repro only with approval"
- "If we need raw logs for a hard bug, create a short-lived support bundle and ask Legal for a one-time exception; record the exception in Jira (SE-7312)."

Open questions / tradeoffs to surface to Product & Privacy:
- How much of the redaction ruleset should be configurable by customers vs managed by Redwood default templates? (config surface area vs safety)
- For Hosted pilots: are we comfortable offering a 14-day debug retention at scale, or should we require Dedicated/Private for any retention >0?
- Deletion certification automation: work to add a self-serve page in Console for pilot deletion requests.

Pilot close checklist (deliverables to customer):
- Deletion certificate (if requested)
- Audit extract: access logs and retention actions (redacted where needed)
- Short report: sample queries/inputs used, summary redactions performed, and recommended production path (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)

Next steps / owners:
- SE owner (Sofia Martinez): finalize scrub util and example repo (action: create PR with se-scrub-util v0.1) — due 2026-02-20.
- Legal liaison (Ellen Park): draft pilot addendum template using the snippet above and circulate to Pilot Legal Ops — due 2026-02-28.
- Product (Marco Li): review feasibility of console self-serve deletion and telemetry opt-in flags — due 2026-03-10.
- Follow-up workshop: schedule 60-minute workshop with customer security to lock retention and KV choices before first run.

Appendix: quick debugging playbook (short form)
1) If customer reports a bad generation potentially containing PII: ask for the minimal repro (hashed identifiers preferred).
2) If SE needs raw inputs: raise a support bundle ticket, get written approval from customer security, store raw bundle with TTL <= 14 days, mark as "support_exception" in Jira.
3) On deletion request: run deletion job for artifacts tagged with pilot-id and deliver deletion certificate.

-- end --

Revision notes: draft v0.1 — created 2025-11-04; iterated after internal pilot review 2026-02-10.
